title: Project Configuration
description: Contract for non-secret Terraform project configuration. Describes one k3s cluster of exactly three dual-role nodes. Cloud-neutral: VMs reference abstract size/image/disk_type/region tiers resolved per-cloud via the *_map dictionaries.

email_recipients.description: Operational alert email recipients. An empty list configures no email recipients.

clouds.description: Explicit probe providers; null retains selection by VM presence.

default_cloud.description: Which cloud this apply targets. Single-cloud-per-apply: every VM in `vms` deploys here.

managed_database.description: Required database hosting selector: true provisions managed PostgreSQL in default_cloud; false runs PostgreSQL in a database-role VM.

managed_kubernetes.description: Kubernetes hosting selector, independent of managed_database: true provisions Amazon EKS, which requires default_cloud aws; false or absent runs the self-hosted k3s cluster described by vms. An omitted key means false, so a configuration written before this key existed keeps deploying k3s.
managed_kubernetes.$comment: Deliberately absent from the required list, unlike managed_database, so older configurations stay valid.

database_profile.description: Key into database_profile_map; used in cloud database mode.

region.description: Key into region_map. Not cross-validated by this schema — an unknown key fails loudly at `terraform plan` via a plain map lookup.

size_map.description: Abstract size tiers (e.g. "small") to native machine/instance type per cloud.

region_map.description: Abstract region keys (e.g. "eu-central") to native region/zone per cloud.

disk_type_map.description: Abstract disk tiers (e.g. "balanced") to native disk/volume type per cloud.

image_map.description: Abstract image keys (e.g. "ubuntu-26.04") to native image reference per cloud. For aws this must be an SSM parameter path starting with /, which the aws module resolves to an AMI ID. Direct AMI IDs are not supported. For azure it is the marketplace publisher/offer/sku/version.

subscription_id.description: Which subscription to deploy into. Not a credential: the token still comes from the environment or az login.

resource_group_name.description: Resource group Terraform creates and owns. The inventory plugin scopes its discovery to it, so it is configuration rather than only an output.

admin_username.description: Which ssh_users entry Azure provisions as the VM's platform administrator. Every other entry is created by cloud-init.

name.description: Globally unique vault name. Omit to derive one from name_prefix, environment, subscription and resource group.

soft_delete_retention_days.description: A deleted vault, and its name, stay reserved for this long.

purge_protection_enabled.description: With purge protection on, a deleted vault cannot be purged early and its name is unavailable for the whole retention period.

subnet_cidr.description: Delegated to Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers and carrying nothing else; /28 or larger, inside vnet_cidr and not overlapping the management or workload subnet.

primary_subnet_cidr.description: Private subnet in the node availability zone.

rds_network.description: Two private subnets for the managed database. RDS requires a subnet group spanning two availability zones, and neither subnet may be the public node subnet.

secondary_subnet_cidr.description: Inside vpc_cidr, overlapping neither the workload subnet nor either rds_network subnet. Not checkable here.

eks_network.description: A second public subnet in a second availability zone. EKS requires the control plane to see at least two zones; the node group and the ingress load balancer stay in the primary zone so the zonal EBS volumes keep reattaching. Required when managed_kubernetes is true.

ui_public_ports.description: Already contains 80, so the ACME HTTP-01 solver needs no additional opening.

registry.description: The selected cloud's native registry: Amazon ECR, Google Artifact Registry or Azure Container Registry, chosen by default_cloud. No credentials live here.

repository_prefix.description: Repository path prefix within the registry, e.g. "oilscope".

publish_tag_prefix.description: Git tag prefix that triggers publishing to this account, e.g. "pavlo-v" for tags pavlo-v1.0.0 onward. The publisher role trusts only refs/tags/<prefix>*, so branch pushes and pull requests cannot publish. The prefix names a destination, not a person: anyone who can push a matching tag can publish here.

create.description: False references an existing registry instead of creating one.

image_digests.description: One immutable digest per built image, named after its Dockerfile in infrastructure/docker. The database image is what the migration Job runs.

github_repository.description: owner/repo allowed to publish through GitHub Actions OIDC. Omit to create no federation and publish only from an operator's machine.

vms.description: The self-hosted k3s nodes: required, and exactly three, when managed_kubernetes is false or absent. Names are free-form; k3s-1, k3s-2 and k3s-3 are the convention. Duplicate internal_ip values are not detectable here - see docs/k3s-deployment.md. Must be absent or empty when managed_kubernetes is true, because an EKS managed node group names no individual machines.

memory_mb.description: Becomes the RabbitMQ container's Kubernetes memory request and limit.

certificate_days.description: Duration of the cert-manager Certificate issued for the broker by the internal CA.

memory_mb.description: Becomes the Redis container's Kubernetes memory request and limit.

actual_thresholds.description: Absolute currency amounts (in the budget's own currency) at which to notify — not fractions of monthly_amount.
Absolute currency amounts (in the budget's own currency) at which to notify — not fractions of monthly_amount.

currency.description: Azure bills in the subscription's own currency and the budget resource takes no currency argument; this records the expected one.

actual_thresholds.description: Absolute currency amounts (in the budget's own currency) at which to notify — not fractions of monthly_amount.

start_date.description: First of a month, UTC. Azure requires a start date and a computed one would replace the budget on every apply.

cloudflare.description: Cloudflare DNS for the UI's public hostname. The API token comes from the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variable, never from this file.

zone_name.description: The apex zone that owns the UI hostname, e.g. "example.com".

ttl.description: Record TTL in seconds: 1 for Cloudflare's automatic value, otherwise 60-86400.

proxied.description: Must stay false: proxying terminates TLS at Cloudflare's edge, so the ACME HTTP-01 solver on port 80 is never reached. Nothing applies this schema automatically - see docs/dns.md.

kubernetes.$comment: Only the keys both hosting modes need are required here. The k3s-only keys (version, entry_node, ssh_address_mode, api_endpoint, pod_cidr, etcd) and the EKS-only key (eks) are required by the managed_kubernetes branches in the root allOf.

version.description: Pinned k3s release, e.g. v1.33.1+k3s1. Ansible installs exactly this; floating channels are not used. Required only when managed_kubernetes is false or absent; the EKS control plane version is kubernetes.eks.version instead.

eks.description: Amazon EKS settings. Required when managed_kubernetes is true, and rejected as unknown otherwise only in the sense that nothing reads it.

version.description: Pinned EKS control plane version, e.g. 1.34. AWS retires versions on its own schedule; an unsupported value fails at apply.

public_api_access.description: Whether the Kubernetes API is reachable from the internet, restricted to admin_allowed_cidrs. Private access is always on as well, which is how nodes reach the API inside the VPC. Turning this off means no operator can reach the cluster without a route into the VPC.

admin_principal_arns.description: Additional IAM roles or users granted cluster administrator access through an EKS access entry. The identity that runs terraform apply is always granted one as well, derived from the caller identity, because the provider defaults bootstrap_cluster_creator_admin_permissions to false and a cluster whose access entries are empty cannot be reached by anybody. Listing the applying identity here is harmless; it is de-duplicated. Name a role rather than a user where possible, and name at least one principal somebody else controls: an access entry is the only way back in, and authentication_mode is API, so there is no aws-auth ConfigMap to edit.

node_group.description: The single managed node group. It runs in the primary availability zone only, so that the zonal EBS volumes RabbitMQ and Redis use can always reattach.

size.description: Key into size_map, resolved through its aws branch exactly as a VM's size is.

capacity_type.description: SPOT nodes can be reclaimed at two minutes' notice, which for single-replica RabbitMQ and Redis means a restart and a volume reattach.

ami_type.description: Must match the architecture of the instance type size_map resolves to, and of every image in registry.image_digests. This schema cannot check either.

entry_node.description: The one node that receives user traffic: both ingress.hostname and api_endpoint resolve to its address. Must name a key in vms, which this schema cannot check. Losing it takes down the website and the API endpoint with no automatic failover.

ssh_address_mode.description: public contacts nodes on their public addresses; private requires an existing route or VPN from the operator's machine.

admin_allowed_cidrs.description: The only sources allowed to reach SSH and the Kubernetes API. There is no bastion; see docs/k3s-recovery.md for the break-glass path when this list stops matching reality.

api_endpoint_mode.description: node connects directly to node addresses without a cloud load balancer, and is the only value k3s accepts. load_balancer is the only value EKS accepts: the API is reached at the endpoint AWS publishes for the cluster.

api_endpoint.description: Hostname clients and kubeconfig use for the Kubernetes API, and a TLS SAN on every server. There is no load balancer: it resolves to all three node addresses, so failover is client retry, not health checking.

pod_cidr.description: Overlap with service_cidr or a subnet is not detectable here and produces a half-working cluster.

snapshot_schedule_cron.description: Offset this per node: one schedule on all three servers makes them take the snapshot and upload cost together.

backup_destination.description: Snapshots cover etcd only. PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ and Redis volumes need their own backups.

headlamp.description: Headlamp, the authenticated operator console. Disabled until an identity provider and a hostname exist. The OIDC client secret is never stored here: it is resolved from the cloud secret container named by oidc.client_secret_secret_id, exactly as the application's runtime secrets are.

hostname.description: Public hostname for the console, e.g. headlamp.example.com. Must differ from ingress.hostname and from kubernetes.api_endpoint; this schema cannot check that. Resolves to the entry node only.

namespace.description: Dedicated namespace for the console. Must not be kubernetes.namespace: the console's runtime identity is deliberately separate from the application's.

chart_version.description: Pinned Headlamp chart version. Overrides the catalogue entry in infrastructure/helm/versions.yml when set.

allowed_cidrs.description: Sources allowed to reach the console at all, enforced by a Traefik IPAllowList in front of authentication. Omit the key to reuse kubernetes.admin_allowed_cidrs; set it to [] to accept every source and rely on the sign-in alone. A changed home address locks the console out exactly as it locks out SSH, and the ACME HTTP-01 challenge is unaffected because cert-manager solves it on its own Ingress.

auth_mode.description: token: operators paste the read-only ServiceAccount's token into Headlamp, and Kubernetes authorises that ServiceAccount. Nothing on the API servers changes. oidc: operators sign in with an identity provider, which additionally requires running configure_k3s_oidc so the API servers validate the issued tokens. Either way the console's own pod holds no cluster permissions.

oidc.description: The identity provider operators sign in with. The same issuer and client ID are given to the k3s API server, so the token Headlamp obtains is the token Kubernetes authorises.

issuer_url.description: OIDC issuer, which must serve a discovery document over HTTPS and be reachable from both the browser and every k3s server.

client_secret_secret_id.description: ID of the secret container holding the client secret. The value is read at deployment time with the operator's own cloud identity and written straight into a Kubernetes Secret; it never reaches this file, Helm values, Terraform state or logs.

scopes.description: Comma separated, as the Headlamp chart expects. Include whichever scope makes the provider emit the groups claim.

username_prefix.description: Prepended by the API server to every authenticated username, so an OIDC identity can never collide with a certificate or service account subject.

groups_claim.description: Claim carrying the operator's groups. Empty means the provider emits none, and the API server is configured without a groups claim; Google ID tokens are the common case. allowed_groups is then unusable and authorisation must name users.

allowed_groups.description: Claim values granted the read-only role, written without the prefix: deployment applies groups_prefix. Leaving both this and allowed_users empty means nobody is authorised, and every sign-in ends in a Kubernetes permission error.

overview.description: Non-secret content for the OilScope Overview landing page. The links are served only to an authenticated operator who may read the overview ConfigMap.

stale_after_seconds.description: A panel older than this is labelled stale rather than presented as current.

url.description: https only. The page drops anything else rather than rendering it.

components.description: The workloads the page expects to exist. One that is absent is reported as not found, never as healthy.

name.description: Suffix appended to name_prefix at deployment time, e.g. "ui" for the oilscope-ui Deployment.

endpoint_mode.description: node exposes ingress directly on node addresses without a cloud load balancer, and is the only value k3s accepts. load_balancer is the only value EKS accepts: Traefik's Service becomes a Network Load Balancer, and the public hostname is a CNAME to it.

hostname.description: Public hostname for the UI, and the name the ingress certificate is issued for. Resolves to all three node addresses; Traefik answers on host ports 80 and 443 on every node.

challenge_type.description: http01 answers on port 80 and needs public DNS pointing at the ingress. dns01 is for private ingress or wildcard certificates.

backup_retention_days.description: Flexible Server accepts 7-35 days; there is no one-day RDS equivalent.

standby_availability_zone.description: Required by ZoneRedundant high availability; null otherwise. Burstable SKUs support no high availability at all.

per_cloud_image.$comment: Images are the one map whose branches are not all strings: an Azure marketplace image is addressed by four coordinates, so it has a definition of its own rather than widening per_cloud_string.

ssh_users.$comment: Maps Linux usernames to public SSH keys. Private keys and local key-file paths are not accepted.

vm_network_tags.description: Both tags, on every node. Membership only: a tag installs nothing. Kubernetes role labels are applied separately by Ansible.

secret_mappings.$comment: Maps application environment variable names to non-secret Secret Manager IDs.

role.description: The only role. Administrative SSH sources are configured once at kubernetes.admin_allowed_cidrs, never per VM.

vm.description: A Kubernetes node. Every node runs a k3s server with embedded etcd and also schedules workloads.

image_digest.description: Immutable image reference. Tags are never deployed.

workload_secret_mappings.description: Secret Manager IDs each workload may read, keyed by workload. Per-workload rather than flat so services keep separate database credentials. rabbitmq and redis are the platform services themselves, which need the credential their clients authenticate with. Names only - never values.
